$comment: TF-C56 (D-CSUBSET-BARE-CHAR-SIGNEDNESS-PER-TARGET): bare `char`'s signedness is target-config-driven — signed on x86_64 (SysV + pe64), UNSIGNED on the two arm64 rows AS DSS CURRENTLY RESOLVES THEM. ONE source; per-target exitCode witnesses the divergence: `char c=(char)0x80; c<0` is TRUE→10 on the signed-char targets, FALSE→20 on the unsigned-char targets. The `volatile` seed defeats const-folding so the release arm runs the real machine char->int extension (SExt vs ZExt/uxtb). ⚠ ABI CORRECTION — an earlier revision of this comment asserted that bare `char` is UNSIGNED on arm64 because the AArch64 ABI says so, and that AAPCS64 and Apple arm64 AGREE. THAT IS FALSE and it is what let the macho row below be written as if it were correct. What is actually true: AAPCS64 and Apple arm64 agree only on the AArch64 *ABI DEFAULT*; AAPCS64 leaves bare-`char` signedness IMPLEMENTATION-DEFINED, the AArch64/GNU-Linux platform ABI chose UNSIGNED, Apple's arm64 platform ABI diverged and chose SIGNED, and clang follows the PLATFORM rather than the architecture. Signedness is therefore an (architecture × PLATFORM) property, not an architecture property. MEASURED BY THIS AGENT 2026-07-28 on Darwin 25.5.0 / arm64 with Apple clang 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101): (a) `clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target aarch64-linux-gnu` defines __CHAR_UNSIGNED__ 1, while `-target arm64-apple-darwin` does NOT define it at all; (b) `_Static_assert((char)-1 < 0)` compiles clean (rc 0) for arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, and FAILS (rc 1, note `(0xFF, 255) < 0`) for aarch64-linux-gnu; (c) on THIS main.c clang emits `ldrsb` (sign-extend) for native arm64-darwin and `ldrb` (zero-extend) under --target=aarch64-linux-gnu. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ROWS BELOW: the two x86_64 rows (10) and the arm64:elf64 row (20) are CORRECT and assert real behaviour. The arm64:macho64 row is NOT — it pins a known DSS defect and carries its own $comment saying so. Read that row's $comment before touching this example.

targets.$comment: ⚠⚠ THIS ROW PINS A KNOWN DSS DEFECT. THE 20 BELOW IS NOT CORRECT BEHAVIOUR — IT IS THE WRONG ANSWER, RECORDED SO THE SUITE STAYS HONEST UNTIL THE FIX LANDS. Anchor: D-TARGET-CHAR-SIGNEDNESS-PER-PLATFORM (OPEN, CONFIRMED). CLANG GROUND TRUTH ON THIS PLATFORM IS 10; THE PINNED DSS VALUE IS 20. MEASURED BY THIS AGENT 2026-07-28 on Darwin 25.5.0 / arm64, every exit code captured DIRECTLY (never after a pipe): Apple clang 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101) compiled this exact main.c and ran it natively → exit 10 at -O0 AND exit 10 at -O2, because bare `char` is SIGNED on arm64-apple-darwin; DSS compiled the same file for arm64:macho64-arm64-darwin-exec and ran it → exit 20 in debug AND exit 20 under --config=release, because DSS treats bare `char` as UNSIGNED here. Same host, same source, same target — 10 vs 20. ROOT CAUSE: `src/dss-config/targets/arm64.target.json` declares a single flat `charIsUnsigned: true` for the whole architecture. That is RIGHT for aarch64-linux-gnu (clang defines __CHAR_UNSIGNED__ there — MEASURED) and WRONG for arm64-apple-darwin (clang does not define it — MEASURED). Bare-`char` signedness is an (architecture × PLATFORM) fact and the `.target.json` key cannot express that split, so the config has no way to say the right thing yet. WHY IT MATTERS: this is a SILENT WRONG-VALUE MISCOMPILE — no diagnostic, no link error, no crash. Every path on macho-arm64 that holds a NEGATIVE bare `char` simply computes a different number than every other compiler on the platform; `(char)0x80 < 0` is false under DSS and true under clang. ⭐ WHEN THE ANCHOR CLOSES, THIS EXPECTATION MUST FLIP 20 → 10. Flipping it is precisely how the fix is proven, so this row is the anchor's closing witness. Do NOT delete this row, do NOT relax it to accept either value, do NOT drop the macho leg, and do NOT weaken any assertion in this example to make a failure here go away — a failure here means either the defect was fixed (then flip to 10) or something regressed (then investigate). The value is 20 ONLY because DSS is currently wrong. ★ STANDING CONSTRAINT while this anchor is open: never use bare-`char` signedness as a runtime architecture/platform cross-check in any other corpus example — such a test would go green on macho-arm64 by AGREEING with this defect and would then break when the defect is fixed.
